subject: math
title: Multiplication as Scaling
seo_title: Grade 5 Multiplication as Scaling Worksheets: Compare Products Without Multiplying, Fractions Greater or Less Than 1
standard_text: Interpret multiplication as scaling (resizing), by: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication. Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number; explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n×a)/(n×b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 worksheets on multiplication as scaling: decide if a product is greater than, less than or equal to a number without multiplying, compare and order products, see equivalent fractions as multiplying by 1, explain mistakes and solve resizing word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Times more than 1 → bigger. Times less than 1 → smaller. Times 1 → the same.
key_sub: 5/4 × 12 = 15 is greater than 12; 3/4 × 12 = 9 is less than 12; 4/4 × 12 = 12. To compare a product with one factor, look at the other factor.
body_html:
The big idea

Multiplying can resize a number. The other factor tells you how:

Multiply byThe product isExample with 12
a number greater than 1greater than 1254 × 12 = 15
a number less than 1less than 1234 × 12 = 9
a number equal to 1equal to 1244 × 12 = 12

A fraction is greater than 1 when the top is greater than the bottom (54), less than 1 when the top is less (34), and equal to 1 when they are the same (44).

See it with bars

Compare without multiplying

To compare a product with one factor, look at the other factor.

Example

Which is greater: 56 × 9 or 76 × 9?

56 is less than 1, so 56 × 9 is less than 9. 76 is greater than 1, so 76 × 9 is greater than 9.

Answer: 76 × 9

Example

Is 34 × 23 greater or less than 23?

Look at the other factor, 34. It is less than 1, so the product is less than 23.

Answer: less than 23

Multiplying by 1 in disguise

22, 33, 44 and 55 are all equal to 1. Multiplying by them does not change the value. It only cuts the parts smaller. That is why equivalent fractions are equal.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
“Multiplying always makes a number bigger.”12 × 10 = 5. Times less than 1 makes it smaller.
“35 × 10 is greater than 34 × 10 because 5 > 4.”A bigger bottom number means smaller parts: 35 < 34
“812 is greater than 23 because 8 > 2.”23 × 44 = 812, and 44 = 1, so they are equal
1 12 × 8 = 8 12Take 8, then add 12 of 8: 8 + 4 = 12

faq.q: What does multiplication as scaling mean?
faq.a: It means thinking of multiplication as resizing a number. Multiplying by a number greater than 1 makes it bigger, by a number less than 1 makes it smaller, and by 1 keeps it the same.

faq.q: Does multiplying by a fraction always make a number smaller?
faq.a: No. Only fractions less than 1 make it smaller: 3/4 × 12 = 9. A fraction greater than 1 makes it bigger: 5/4 × 12 = 15.

faq.q: How can you compare products without multiplying?
faq.a: Look at the other factor. 5/6 × 9 is less than 9 because 5/6 is less than 1, and 7/6 × 9 is greater than 9 because 7/6 is greater than 1.

faq.q: Why does multiplying by 4/4 give an equivalent fraction?
faq.a: 4/4 is equal to 1, and multiplying by 1 does not change a number. So 2/3 × 4/4 = 8/12 is the same amount as 2/3, cut into smaller parts.

sets.title: Greater than, less than or equal to the number?

items.q: The top bar is 12. The bottom bar shows 34 × 12. Without multiplying, how does 34 × 12 compare with 12?
items.e: 34 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so 34 × 12 is less than 12. It is only part of 12. You do not need to multiply. In the picture, the bottom bar has 3 equal parts and the top bar has 4.

items.q: The top bar is 8. The bottom bar shows 54 × 8. Without multiplying, how does 54 × 8 compare with 8?
items.e: 54 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom), so 54 × 8 is greater than 8. It is more than 1 group of 8. You do not need to multiply. In the picture, the bottom bar has 5 equal parts and the top bar has 4.

items.q: Without multiplying, is 4 × 25 greater than, less than or equal to 25?

items.q: Without multiplying, is 34 × 56 greater than, less than or equal to 56?
items.e: Compare the product with 56 by looking at the other factor, 34. 34 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so the product is less than 56.

items.q: Without multiplying, is 34 × 56 greater than, less than or equal to 34?
items.e: Compare the product with 34 by looking at the other factor, 56. 56 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so the product is less than 34. (It does not matter that 34 is also less than 1.)

items.q: Without multiplying, is 1 15 × 37 greater than, less than or equal to 37?
items.e: Compare the product with 37 by looking at the other factor, 1 15. 1 15 is greater than 1, so the product is greater than 37.

items.q: Which product is less than 15?
items.e: 78 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so 78 × 15 is less than 15. Check the others: 98 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom); 1515 is equal to 1 (the top and the bottom are the same); 1 14 is greater than 1.

items.q: Which product is greater than 24?
items.e: 53 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom), so 53 × 24 is greater than 24. Check the others: 35 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom); 88 is equal to 1 (the top and the bottom are the same); 99100 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom).

items.q: Which product is equal to 9?
items.e: 77 is equal to 1 (the top and the bottom are the same), so 77 × 9 is equal to 9. Check the others: 97 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom); 79 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom); 1 17 is greater than 1.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is greater: 56 × 9 or 76 × 9?
items.e: 76 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom), so 76 × 9 is more than 9. 56 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so 56 × 9 is less than 9. The greater one is 76 × 9.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is greater: 34 × 10 or 35 × 10?
items.e: Both products multiply 10. 34 is greater than 35 because fourths are larger parts than fifths. A greater factor makes a greater product, so 34 × 10 is greater.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is greater: 45 × 16 or 54 × 16?
items.e: 54 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom), so 54 × 16 is more than 16. 45 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so 45 × 16 is less than 16. The greater one is 54 × 16.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is greater: 87 × 14 or 78 × 14?
items.e: 87 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom), so 87 × 14 is more than 14. 78 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so 78 × 14 is less than 14. The greater one is 87 × 14.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is greater: 1 12 × 6 or 1 13 × 6?
items.e: Both products multiply 6. 1 12 is greater than 1 13 because halves are larger parts than thirds. A greater factor makes a greater product, so 1 12 × 6 is greater.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is greater: 910 × 30 or 1 110 × 30?
items.e: 1 110 is greater than 1, so 1 110 × 30 is more than 30. 910 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so 910 × 30 is less than 30. The greater one is 1 110 × 30.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is greater: 66 × 11 or 11?
items.e: 66 is equal to 1 (the top and the bottom are the same), so 66 × 11 = 11. They are equal.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is greater: 23 × 21 or 23 × 15?
items.e: Both are 23 of a number. 23 of a greater number is greater, so 23 × 21 is greater.

items.q:
A = 23 × 30, B = 76 × 30, C = 25 × 30
Without multiplying, order the products from least to greatest.
items.e: All three products multiply 30, so order the factors: 25 < 23 < 76. So the order is C, A, B. A bigger bottom number does not make a bigger fraction: fifths are smaller than thirds.

items.q:
A = 54 × 16, B = 58 × 16, C = 88 × 16
Without multiplying, order the products from least to greatest.
items.e: All three products multiply 16, so order the factors: 58 < 88 < 54. So the order is B, C, A. Eighths are smaller than fourths, so 58 is less than 54.

items.q:
A = 310 × 50, B = 910 × 50, C = 1 110 × 50
Without multiplying, order the products from least to greatest.
items.e: All three products multiply 50, so order the factors: 310 < 910 < 1 110. So the order is A, B, C. 1 110 is the only factor greater than 1.

items.q:
A = 34 × 12, B = 34 × 8, C = 54 × 12
Without multiplying, order the products from least to greatest.
items.e: A and B are both 34 of a number, and 8 < 12, so B < A. A is less than 12 (34 < 1) and C is more than 12 (54 > 1), so A < C. The order is B, A, C.

items.q: ? × 25 is greater than 25. Which number could be in the box?
items.e: The product is greater than 25, so the box must be greater than 1. 98 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom). Check the others: 89 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom); 66 is equal to 1 (the top and the bottom are the same); 12 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom).

items.q: ? × 18 is less than 18. Which number could be in the box?

items.q: ? × 7 is equal to 7. Which number could be in the box?
items.e: The product is equal to 7, so the box must be equal to 1. 33 is equal to 1 (the top and the bottom are the same). Check the others: 17 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom); 34 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom); 43 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom).

items.q: ? × 8 is between 4 and 8. Which number could be in the box?
items.e: To be less than 8, the box must be less than 1. To be more than 4 (half of 8), it must be more than 12. 34 is between 12 and 1. (14 × 8 = 2, 12 × 8 = 4 and 54 × 8 = 10 are not between 4 and 8.)

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 1?
items.e: A fraction is equal to 1 when the top and the bottom are the same: 66 = 1. (61 = 6 and 16 is less than 1.)

items.q: 23 × 44 = ?

sets.title: Explain why and find the mistake

items.q: Why is 74 × 9 greater than 9?
c: 74 is greater than 1
items.e: 74 is greater than 1, so 74 × 9 is more than 1 group of 9. So the reason is: 74 is greater than 1. (Multiplying does not always make things bigger: 12 × 9 is less than 9.)

items.q: Why is 38 × 50 less than 50?
c: 38 is less than 1
38 × 50 means 50 − 38
items.e: 38 is less than 1, so 38 × 50 is only part of 50. Not all fractions make numbers smaller: 98 × 50 is more than 50.

items.q: Ruby says, “Multiplying always makes a number bigger.” Which example shows that she is wrong?
items.e: In 12 × 10 = 5, the product 5 is less than 10. When you multiply by a number less than 1, the product is smaller. The other examples all get bigger.

items.q: Which statement is always true?
c: A number times a fraction is always smaller
A number times a fraction less than 1 is less than the number
A product is always greater than both factors
A bigger denominator makes a bigger product
items.e: Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 takes only part of the number, so the product is smaller. Fractions greater than 1, such as 54, make it bigger, and a bigger denominator means smaller parts.

items.q: Sofia says 23 × 18 = 27. Without multiplying, how do you know her answer is wrong?
c: The product must be less than 18
The product must be more than 27
items.e: 23 is less than 1, so 23 × 18 must be less than 18. 27 is more than 18, so it cannot be right. (27 is 18 ÷ 23. The product is 12.)

items.q: Ben says 59 × 20 is greater than 56 × 20 because 9 is greater than 6. What is his mistake?
items.e: A bigger bottom number means smaller parts. 59 is less than 56, so 59 × 20 is less than 56 × 20.

items.q: Zoe says 34 × 44 = 1216, so the product is greater than 34. What is true?
c: 1216 is less than 34
She should add 34 + 44
44 = 1, so 1216 = 34
items.e: 44 is 1, and multiplying by 1 does not change a number. 1216 is equal to 34: it has more parts, but each part is smaller.

items.q: Noah multiplied a number by 56 and got 30. Was the number he started with more or less than 30?
items.e: Multiplying by 56 (less than 1) makes a number smaller. The product 30 is smaller than the start, so the start was more than 30. (It was 36: 56 × 36 = 30.)

items.q: Leo multiplied a number by 43 and got 20. Was the number he started with more or less than 20?
items.e: Multiplying by 43 (greater than 1) makes a number bigger. The product 20 is bigger than the start, so the start was less than 20. (It was 15: 43 × 15 = 20.)

items.q: Eli says 1 12 × 8 = 8 12. What is his mistake?
c: He added 12 instead of taking 12 of 8
The product should be less than 8
items.e: 1 12 × 8 is 1 group of 8 and 12 of 8 more: 8 + 4 = 12. He added 12 instead of taking 12 of 8.

items.q: Is 34 × 23 greater or less than 23? Which reason is right?
c: Less, because 34 is less than 1
Less, because 23 is less than 1
items.e: To compare the product with 23, look at the other factor, 34. 34 is less than 1, so the product is less than 23. (23 being less than 1 tells you about comparing with 34, not with 23.)

items.q: Without multiplying, how do you know that 6 × 45 is greater than 45?
c: 45 is less than 1
items.e: 6 × 45 is 6 groups of 45. The other factor, 6, is greater than 1, so the product is greater than 45.

items.q: Any number is multiplied by 77. Which is true about the product?
c: It is greater than the number
It is less than the number
items.e: 77 = 1, and a number times 1 is the same number. So the product equals the number.

items.q: Which product is less than both of its factors?
c: 23 × 34
items.e: Both 23 and 34 are less than 1, so each one makes the other smaller. 23 × 34 = 12 is less than both. 4 × 12 = 2 is less than 4 but greater than 12.

items.q: Which product is greater than both of its factors?
c: 12 × 32
items.e: Both 32 and 4 are greater than 1, so each one makes the other bigger: 32 × 4 = 6. 23 × 6 = 4 is less than 6, and 1 × 5 = 5 is not greater than 5.

items.q: Mia says 910 × 40 is close to 40, but a little less. Is she right?
c: Yes: 910 is a little less than 1
No: it is a lot less than 40
items.e: 910 is just a little less than 1, so 910 × 40 is a little less than 40. (It is 36.)

items.q: Owen says 25 × 35 is greater than 12 × 35. Is he right?
c: No: 25 is less than 12
Yes: fifths are greater than halves
items.e: 25 is less than 12 (2 out of 5 is less than half of 5), so 25 × 35 is less than 12 × 35.

items.q: a × 12 = 12. What do you know about a?
items.e: The product is the same as 12, so a did not change it: a = 1 (for example, 55).

items.q: b × 15 is less than 15. What do you know about b?
items.e: Only a factor less than 1 makes 15 smaller. (A number less than 15, such as 2, makes 2 × 15 = 30.)

items.q: c × 35 is greater than 35. What do you know about c?
c: It is greater than 35
items.e: Only a factor greater than 1 makes 35 bigger. Greater than 35 is not enough: 45 × 35 is less than 35.

items.q: Luis has a photo that is 6 inches wide. He prints a copy 1 12 times as wide. How wide is the copy?
items.e: The copy is 1 12 times 6 inches. 1 12 is greater than 1, so the answer must be greater than 6 inches. 1 12 × 6 = 9 inches. (1 × 6 = 6, and 12 of 6 is 3 more.)

items.q: A poster is 8 feet tall. Kai makes a small copy that is 34 as tall. How tall is the small copy?
items.e: The copy is 34 of 8 feet. 34 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so the answer must be less than 8 feet. 34 × 8 = 6 feet.

items.q: A muffin recipe uses 3 cups of flour. Jack makes 23 of the recipe. How much flour does he use?
items.e: Jack uses 23 of 3 cups. 23 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so the answer must be less than 3 cups. 23 × 3 = 2 cups.

items.q: A pancake recipe uses 2 cups of milk. Omar makes 1 12 batches. How much milk does he need?
items.e: 1 12 batches use 1 12 times 2 cups. 1 12 is greater than 1, so the answer must be greater than 2 cups. 1 12 × 2 = 3 cups.

items.q: A real whale is 72 feet long. A model of the whale is 124 as long. How long is the model?
items.e: The model is 124 of 72 feet. 124 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so the answer must be less than 72 feet. 124 × 72 = 3 feet. (72 ÷ 24 = 3.)

items.q: On a map, 1 inch stands for 8 miles. Two towns are 2 12 inches apart on the map. How far apart are the real towns?
items.e: The real distance is 2 12 times 8 miles. 2 12 is greater than 1, so the answer must be greater than 8 miles. 2 12 × 8 = 20 miles. (2 × 8 = 16, and 12 of 8 is 4 more.)

items.q: Sam ran 3 miles on Monday. On Tuesday, he ran 23 as far. How far did he run on Tuesday?
items.e: Tuesday is 23 of 3 miles. 23 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so the answer must be less than 3 miles. 23 × 3 = 2 miles.

items.q: A soup recipe uses 4 cups of broth. Emma makes 1 12 times the recipe for a party. How much broth does she need?
items.e: Emma needs 1 12 times 4 cups. 1 12 is greater than 1, so the answer must be greater than 4 cups. 1 12 × 4 = 6 cups.

items.q: Painting a big wall takes 3 gallons of paint. A smaller wall is 56 the size. How much paint does the smaller wall take?
items.e: The smaller wall needs 56 of 3 gallons. 56 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so the answer must be less than 3 gallons. 56 × 3 = 2 12 gallons. (3 ÷ 6 = 12, and 5 × 12 = 2 12.)

items.q: Lily's walk to school takes 12 minutes. Riding a bike takes 34 as long. How long does the bike ride take?
items.e: The bike ride takes 34 of 12 minutes. 34 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so the answer must be less than 12 minutes. 34 × 12 = 9 minutes. (12 ÷ 4 = 3, and 3 × 3 = 9.)

items.q: Nora's puppy weighs 12 pounds. In a few months, it will weigh 2 12 times as much. How much more will it weigh then?
items.e: 2 12 is greater than 1, so the puppy will get heavier: 2 12 × 12 = 24 + 6 = 30 pounds (2 × 12 = 24, and 12 of 12 is 6). That is 30 − 12 = 18 pounds more. (30 pounds is the new weight, not how much more.)

items.q: Maya has a banner that is 24 inches wide. She shrinks it to 56 of its width. How much narrower is the new banner?
items.e: 56 is less than 1, so the banner gets narrower: 56 × 24 = 20 inches. That is 24 − 20 = 4 inches narrower. (16 of 24 is 4.)

items.q: A garden bed is 12 feet long. A new bed will be 76 as long. How much longer is the new bed?
items.e: 76 is greater than 1, so the new bed is longer: 76 × 12 = 14 feet. That is 14 − 12 = 2 feet longer. (The extra 16 of 12 is 2.)

items.q: A sunflower is 10 cm tall. Next week it will be 1 14 times as tall. Which is true?
c: It will be shorter than 10 cm
It will be taller than 10 cm
It will be 1 14 cm taller
items.e: 1 14 is greater than 1, so the sunflower will be taller than 10 cm. It grows by 14 of 10 cm (2 12 cm), not by 1 14 cm.

items.q: Ava makes 34 of a cookie recipe. Ruby makes 54 of the same recipe. Who uses more sugar?
items.e: 34 is less than 1 and 54 is greater than 1, so Ruby uses more. You do not need to know how much sugar the recipe uses.

items.q: A bottle holds 34 liter of water. Sofia drinks 23 of it. Without multiplying, how much does she drink?
c: More than 34 liter
Less than 34 liter
items.e: 23 is less than 1, so 23 of 34 liter is less than 34 liter. (It is 12 liter.)

items.q: Ben wants to make a photo smaller. Which could he multiply its width by?
items.e: To make it smaller, multiply by a number less than 1: 45. 54 and 1 12 make it bigger, and 66 keeps it the same.

items.q: A giraffe is 18 feet tall. A tree is 1 13 times as tall as the giraffe. A bush is 13 as tall as the giraffe. Which list goes from shortest to tallest?
items.e: The bush is 13 of 18 (less than 18), the tree is 1 13 times 18 (more than 18). So the order is bush, giraffe, tree: 6 ft, 18 ft, 24 ft.

items.q: Zoe draws a rectangle 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. Then she draws a copy that is 1 12 times as long on each side. What are the sides of the copy?
c: 7 12 cm and 5 12 cm
4 cm and 2 23 cm
6 12 cm and 4 12 cm
items.e: 1 12 is greater than 1, so both sides get longer. 1 12 × 6 = 6 + 3 = 9 and 1 12 × 4 = 4 + 2 = 6. The copy is 9 cm and 6 cm. (Do not add 1 12 or 12 to each side.)

items.q: Noah copies a drawing at 23 size. Then he copies the copy at 32 size. How does the last copy compare with the first drawing?
items.e: 23 × 32 = 66, and 66 = 1. Multiplying by 1 does not change the size, so the last copy is the same size as the first drawing.
